title: The Night Mail
hook: My landlord had one rule about the mail slot: if anything comes through after dark, don't open it. Burn it.
lines: My new apartment had a brass mail slot in the front door... and one rule from the landlord.
Mail only comes in the morning. If anything drops through after dark... don't open it. Burn it.
For a whole month, that slot never moved after sunset.
Then, one night, in the middle of a thunderstorm... I heard it creak open.
A single envelope slid onto the floor.
No stamp. No address. Just my name... written in my own handwriting.
I knelt down. The brass flap was still being held open... from the hallway.
Something out there was breathing through it. Slow. Patient. Waiting for me to read.
I burned that letter in the sink, unopened. The flap snapped shut. Footsteps went down the stairs.
This morning, my neighbor knocked. She was holding an open envelope. Her hands were shaking.
It came through my slot last night, she whispered. In your handwriting. It says... she won't read mine.
Then she leaned in close... breathing slow and patient... and asked if she could come in.
end_card: Never let anyone read it for you.
